correctness.rationale: Support directions of a regular heptagon reduce to 14 discrete normals. The supporting-polygon area identity follows by triangulation around the interior origin. All 511 admissible four-line enclosures are exhaustively compared with outward-rounded rational intervals from rigorous Taylor/Machin bounds. Seven equal-area edge-supported winners are analytically evaluated, and each of 504 competitors is separated by >1/40. Third-order root identity is checked by exact substitution. The finite certificate is genuinely exhaustive after the geometric reduction; no infinite conclusion rests on sampling.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The universal upper bounds guarantee existence of some enclosing quadrilateral but neither evaluate a particular heptagon's exact minimum nor force an optimizing support orbit. The closed formula for enclosing parallelograms cannot imply the smaller optimum over non-parallelogram chord quadrilaterals.

The exact algebraic constant, complete symmetry-rigid optimizer classification and certified positive gap distinguish the phase of supported directions and create a reproducible sharp finite benchmark for extremal polygon enclosure. This is not a proof of a general conjecture; the narrower complete classification has independent geometric content.
